text:
noah: Working from the garage today because my apartment is being painted. Its actually nice but when it started raining the laptop beeped and Zoom got choppy. Posted a pic of my makeshift garage desk: https://files.slack.com/archives/random/FGAR1234/GARAGE1.jpg

reena: Garage office energy. Quick tip: keep the laptop elevated on a hard surface to avoid damp and to help cooling. Also put a towel under it if the floor is cold/wet.

owen: If you're getting drops during rain, might be interference or your ISP's last-mile. Try tethering to your phone as a hotspot and disable wifi on the laptop to force cellular.

noah: I tried tether, better but not perfect. Any small hardware thats low-effort? Dont want to lug an AP out there.

maya: I used a travel router with a USB LTE stick once. Setup was 5 minutes and it isolated the garage traffic. Otherwise, a long ethernet run to the window + short patch cable is the fastest stable fix.

signal-bot: Tip: "For short ethernet runs, use a USB3-to-Ethernet adapter if your laptop lacks a port. Run the cable through a slightly opened window and seal with towel to keep weather out." :robot_face:

reena: Also check background syncers (Dropbox/OneDrive) - they love to kick in and take bandwidth when they notice new files. Pause them during calls.

owen: If the rain causes power fluctuations, plug your router into a small UPS or at least a surge protector. Nothing worse than router reboot mid-demo.

noah: Quick question: is there an easy way to check if the router is the problem vs ISP? Ran `ping 8.8.8.8 -t` and saw spikes during the rain. Is that usually ISP?

reena: Spikes usually indicate ISP or line noise, but test: plug directly into modem (bypass router) with ethernet if you can. If spikes persist, call ISP. If stable, the router/AP might be choking under interference.

owen: Another quick test: run a traceroute during a spike to see the first hop that jumps latency. On mac/linux: `traceroute 8.8.8.8`, on Windows: `tracert 8.8.8.8`.

noah: Did a direct modem test and spikes still there. Called ISP and they said "maintenance in the area"  good to know. Tethered for rest of meeting and everything was fine. Will test again after work. Thanks for the gear ideas though  might get a travel AP if painting keeps dragging on.

maya: Pro bonus: if you end up with a travel AP, name the SSID something subtle like "garage-net-guest" so you don't accidentally share access with neighbors.

signal-bot: Tip: "When using hotspot, plug the phone into power and enable do-not-disturb to avoid interruptions. If possible, set the phone to 5G/4G LTE only to avoid Wi-Fi handoff weirdness." :robot_face:

noah: Victory note: packed up before a heavy downpour started. Router survived and painting crew didnt flood my laptop. Will post the full garage-office before/after tomorrow. Also very tempted to turn this into a weekend project. Thanks y'all!
